model_object.display_name: The modelled EWSR1 e7 :: NR4A3 e3 construct

definition.exon_level: EWSR1 exon 7 :: NR4A3 exon 3 — ⛔ NOT A REPORTED FUSION TYPE. It pairs the 5′ half of reported type 2 with the 3′ half of reported type 1.
definition.residue_level: EWSR1(1–264) :: NR4A3(1–626), with no UTR-encoded segment

distinct_from.why: shares type 2's 5′ cut only, and omits type 2's 59 UTR-encoded residues

model_object.notes: ⚠ THE NAME 'the canonical EMC fusion' WAS ATTACHED TO THIS MODEL and to OBJ-FUS-T1 in different files — see contested_names. What the correction does NOT disturb: the arithmetic for a 264-residue EWSR1 cut is still valid, and it is still the right comparator for EWSR1::FLI1 type 1, which really does cut at 264. What changes is the LABEL. Superseded figures quoted off this object stay quotable via emc-atr-collaborator-package.md's appendix. ⚠ THE `emc_canonical_EWSR1_NR4A3` ALIAS IS HISTORICAL AS OF 2026-09-02 (AUT-PD-208): emc-fet-idr-census.json no longer writes that key. It now carries every reported EWSR1::NR4A3 type under `emc_EWSR1_NR4A3_reported_types`, keyed by the sourced registry's ids, so the exon-7 record sits under `EWSR1_NR4A3_type2` and asserts nothing about which type is commonest. The alias is kept so the retired name stays searchable.

integrity_conflict.what: 'the canonical EMC fusion' names two incompatible objects, and one working module is built on the one that is not a reported fusion type.
positions: emc-atr-collaborator-package.md §2.2 + appendix: 'canonical' now belongs to reported type 1 (EWSR1 e12 :: NR4A3 e3); the e7::e3 combination is not a reported type. The e7::e3 ARITHMETIC remains valid and remains the right comparator for EWSR1::FLI1 type 1.
Same file §7.2: reported type 2 carries 59 UTR-encoded residues, so fusion_cofold.py's protein-level model (EWS_CUT = 264, 'NR4A3 resumed at res 2') is not type 2 either.
Same file, appendix: the §1.3 off-by-two correction is NOT superseded — both reported types retain NR4A3 from its first coding exon, so AF-1, the C4 zinc finger and the LBD are present under either.
integrity_conflict.why_not_decided: Changing which junction fusion_cofold.py models is a science decision with downstream reach (the neoantigen lane's seams, the IDR census's canonical row, R13's object) and at least three modules would have to move together. The registry's job is to make the three models nameable and separable; choosing between them is not a navigation-layer call.
